title: iterative-light-canary-protocols-for-multi-tenant-inference-draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, low-ceremony canary and A/B playbook designed for multi-tenant inference surfaces (hosted API + Dedicated). Goal: reduce cognitive load for small teams, enable safe fast iteration, and provide deterministic rollback criteria that operations and SRE can act on without heavy data wrangling.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: low-latency endpoints and routing changes that affect model selection, quantization profile, or batching policy per-tenant.
- Not for schema-level or infra-control-plane changes (those follow full SRE runbook).
- Assumes standard telemetry: per-tenant p50/p95 token latency, error-rate (4xx/5xx), token counts, cost-per-token estimate, and a quality trace sample (random sample of responses).
- For A/B experiments, metric hooks to the evaluation service (async scoring) are required before exposure.

Quick summary (one-line protocol):
1) Localize change to a small cohort (single-tenant or 1% traffic slice), 2) run synthetic and sampled live tests for 60–90 minutes, 3) evaluate signal thresholds (latency/error/quality), 4) expand or rollback.

Roles and responsibilities (lightweight):
- Owner: product or ML engineer who authored the change — responsible for hypothesis, initial signal checks, and first-level rollback.
- Steward: release steward (rotation) from rollout-ops — watches dashboards and triggers escalation if signals degrade.
- SRE on-call: quick validation if infra/system resources are implicated.
- CS/Customer-success: notified for tenant-visible changes if tenant is >10% MRR.

Pre-checklist before exposure (preflight):
- Small synthetic load test: run 30s to 5m synthetic traffic that mirrors the 95th percentile request path for the tenant. Capture latency and error.
- Unit smoke: run previously recorded golden prompts (5-10) through the change for functional drift.
- Simulation: if routing change, validate fallback paths are wired and responses still decode correctly (no schema break).
- Change description and rollback plan documented in the linear ticket.

Exposure plan template (use copy/paste):
- Cohort definition: tenant(s) or slice by header "canary-version=alpha"
- Initial exposure: 1% traffic or single tenant; duration 60 minutes
- Expand plan: double every 60m if all checks pass -> 1% -> 2% -> 4% -> 8% -> 25% -> 100% (stop at business gate if >10% change)
- Safety hold: any severe signal triggers immediate hold and 10-minute review.

Signals and thresholds (operational):
- Latency: +p95 increase > 30% absolute AND +p50 increase > 15% -> warn.
- Errors: 5xx spike > 0.5% absolute or 4xx spike correlated with a known validation issue -> critical.
- Cost: expected per-token cost delta > +20% for sustained 30 min -> review.
- Quality: automated BLEU/ROUGE-like metric or eval score drop > 8% relative to baseline on evaluation set -> warn. If coupled with user-visible drop in manual samples -> critical.
- Availability: if any tenant experiences >3 min continuous failure -> critical.

Observability checklist (what steward watches):
- Per-slice latency heatmap (p50/p90/p95), error-rate time series, request volume, model instance CPU/GPU util, cache hit-rate, and KV latency.
- Sampled traces with full prompt+response for drift inspection.
- Cost estimator rolling window (last 60m).

Rollback guide (fast path):
- Owner triggers "revert-routing" flag in console (automated rollback) or reassign route to prior model variant.
- Communicate in #rollout-ops: "rollback executed: <ticket>, reason: <short reason>, time"
- Postmortem triggers if rollback due to critical signal or if user impact > 10k requests.

Light experiment design notes (A/B for quality):
- Always pair automated eval set with live sample inspection. Eval sets should be small (200–1k examples) but targeted to high-risk prompts (safety, hallucination-prone queries).
- Use stratified sampling by tenant size and traffic shape.
- Avoid monolithic metrics — prefer composite gates (latency+error+quality) to reduce false positives.

Communication templates (to copy into Slack/Emails):
- Pre-exposure: "Heads-up: rolling canary for <feature> to slice <cohort>. Owner: @<owner>. Initial exposure 1% at <time>. Watch: latency p95, 5xx% and eval score. Linear: <ticket>"
- On hold: "Hold: expanding canary paused at <stage>. Observed signal: <metric> exceeded threshold. Owner investigating."
- Rollback: "Rollback executed for <feature>. Trigger: <metric> exceeded. Reverted to <version>. Postmortem ticket: <ticket>"

Synthetic traffic recipes (for quick stress):
- Short-burst: 200 concurrent requests over 30s with 95th-prompt-length sequences to exercise attention and KV cache.
- Mixed-load: 60s with 50% short prompts, 30% medium, 20% long to mirror production mix.
- Edge-case flood: repeated malformed prompts / heavy token generation to validate graceful degradation and timeouts.

Low-friction telemetry checks (quick commands):
- Sanity query to sample 50 responses: `scripts/sample_canary_responses --slice=alpha --n=50`
- Quick perf health: `observability/query --metric=p95_latency --slice=alpha --window=60m`
- Automated eval runner: `evals/run --suite=canary-smoke --version=canary`

Open questions / work items (short backlog):
- How to automatically tie quality eval deltas to staging traffic expansion decisions? (rule engine or manual?)
- Add lightweight per-tenant GAU (golden acceptance unit) tests that run preflight on deploy.
- Explore burst-aware expansion pacing (avoid doubling when backend GPU pool is in busy state).

Notes to self / scraps:
- Keep canary exposure windows as multiples of 60m for human monitoring alignment.
- For Dedicated customers, gating must include account CS notification BEFORE expanding past 10% traffic.
- Consider a one-click "quarantine" that isolates failing tenants and redirects them to fallback model variant.

Immediate next steps (for this doc):
- Share with stewardship rotation (Asha, Liam) for feedback.
- Prototype a Linear workflow that auto-posts metrics snapshot on each expansion stage.
- Draft a terse console UI microcopy for the canary flow (owner, steward, rollback button).

References and links:
- Linear ticket: INF-842 (linked above)
- Related runbooks: short-runbook link in console docs (TODO fill)

End of draft.

-- Jordan (notes)
